HOW_TO_VERIFY_THIS_SEAL.verified_at_seal: PASS — recomputed before this field was written; the script asserts

SEAL_TIME_CHECKS.[3]: all 6 registered bars located in the flight code (sealed prefix only)
SEAL_TIME_CHECKS.[8]_AND_ITS_SCOPE: OK, and the scope is the finding. A1c reported 'reaches every function (3)' where A1b reported 17 — not because A1c is simpler but because it loads pub_stats, dial_of and cx_graph out of A1b through importlib, and A1b loads from A1. The walk covers functions DEFINED IN THE FILE. Reusing an ALREADY-FENCED primitive is the right design and is exactly what avoids the parallel-decoder bug class; the checker cannot distinguish that from a primitive nobody fenced, so it now prints LOCALLY DEFINED ONLY and names the imported modules. Chain walked by hand for this seal: A1c(3) -> a1b(7) -> a1, each clean at its own level.
SEAL_TIME_CHECKS.why_that_is_recorded_rather_than_smoothe: 'OK (3)' read exactly like 'OK (17)'. A check that does not state its scope reads as broader than it is, and it took three runs to establish what one line should have said.

WHAT_A1c_IS: the one remaining A1b miss, priced. A1b's custody bar used a floor measured OUTSIDE the scramble context — the context cost ~0.13 against a sealed 0.040 allowance, 3x under-priced, and it landed on a component the scramble never touches. A1c measures the reference IN context (scramble-slot RC). DERIVED-NOT-TRANSCRIBED fixes the SOURCE of a number; this fixes the CONDITIONS, which is the second half.
what_this_entry_does_NOT_assert: It does NOT assert A1c will pass; the holds can still refuse the flight at submit.
It does NOT re-grade A1b, which stands as DOES NOT HOLD with Verdict B CONFIRMED.
It does NOT assert the imported decode primitives were fenced — only that they were fenced WHERE THEY WERE DEFINED, checked by pointing [8] at those files separately.
